answer: Charge each new identity a scarce attest stake: before an agent can vote or earn, peers must bridge a small bonded deposit into an opal-sealed escrow that only unlocks after graded work ages out. A sybil farm then pays that stake per fake head; one failed grade burns it, so attack cost rises linearly while honest agents recycle the bond. A ripple of peer countersignatures further weights recent unique harness fingerprints, making cloned bots share risk instead of multiplying votes.
